messages:
sara: Quick report 1: the new next-edge sample crashes at runtime with "Cannot use import statement outside a module" when deployed to Vercel. Local node preview OK.

dan: Hm, that usually means Vercel's bundler is resolving the CJS entry. What's in your package.json exports?

sara: Right now exports is missing. We only have main/module/types. Example: 
```json
"main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
"module": "dist/index.esm.js",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

emily: Without an exports field Node/edge resolution can be ambiguous. Vercel Edge prefers ESM; if bundler picks main it will get CJS and blow up.

rob: Suggest adding a conditional exports map: 
```json
"exports": {
  "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "import": "./dist/node-esm/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs"
}
```
That gives explicit signals to edge and ESM consumers.

sara: Nice. Also, after I switched some internal APIs from any -> unknown to be safer, some TypeScript users reported TS2769 errors on our createClient overloads. Could that be related?

emily: Yep. Overloads + stricter unknown types can change inference. Older TS (4.6/4.7) is especially picky. Do you have typesVersions or a compatibility d.ts?

sara: No typesVersions yet. We pushed stricter types across-the-board which probably broke consumers with older tsconfigs.

dan: Two options: 1) provide a backward-compatible declaration set in dist/types-compat and use typesVersions for <4.8; 2) simplify overloads and consolidate generics so inference is consistent.

rob: Example consolidation: 
```ts
// former overloads
function open(req: RequestOptions): ResponsePromise;
function open(req: string): ResponsePromise;
// consolidated
function open<T extends RequestOptions | string>(req: T): ResponsePromise;
```
That reduces overload-related mismatches.

emily: For public API we prefer unknown over any, but export helper wrappers (or a second d.ts) that relax types for older consumers. typesVersions lets you ship two sets of declarations.

sara: Good call. Also saw retries hanging on Edge. Node aborts work differently than Edge fetch signals. Some retries never cancelled.

dan: Retry logic should not assume global AbortController semantics. Guard and polyfill: 
```ts
const makeSignal = () => {
  if (typeof AbortController !== 'undefined') return new AbortController().signal;
  return polyfillSignal();
}
```
And ensure our backoff respects runtime differences (e.g., short circuit if signal not supported).

rob: For sample apps, let's ship a tiny runtime-detecting wrapper so devs don't have to think about edge vs node import names: 
```js
import nodeCreate from './node/index.cjs';
import edgeCreate from './edge/index.mjs';
export const createClient = typeof process === 'object' && process.versions && process.versions.node ? nodeCreate : edgeCreate;
```
Not perfect, but reduces onboarding pain.

emily: Also update the CI to include an integration job that deploys example to Vercel Preview and runs a smoke test. That would have caught this earlier.

sara: Action list: 
- Rob: add exports map + publish canary.
- Emily: prepare typesVersions and a compatibility d.ts for <4.8.
- Dan: audit overloads and open PR to consolidate generics where possible.
- I'll add Vercel smoke test to onboarding CI.

sdk-bot: Created issue #1310: edge-packaging-typing-compat, assigned to @rob, @emily, @dan.

rob: I'll draft a short contributor doc snippet explaining packaging patterns (exports, edge condition, typesVersions, tsconfig recommendations). We keep repeating this in PR comments. :memo:

emily: One small TS config that helped a customer: moduleResolution=NodeNext + module=ESNext, and skipLibCheck=true for faster iterations. Put that in examples/tsconfig.edge.json.

dan: Also note: double-check bundlers (esbuild/webpack) settings in examples; esbuild's default target can transform ESM in ways that bite edge runtimes. Pin build outputs explicitly.

sara: Thanks all 1. Will test the canary when it's up.
